reviewer.role: independent bounded CODE-PROOF retained I/O, Git object and configuration semantics reviewer

verdict: R2 preserves the intended zero-egress boundary, fixed one-request/intent/observation batch, deterministic repair direction, separate normalized-only mode, SHA-1/SHA-256 Git framing and the tighter object/config limits. It is not ready for schema or allowlist freeze because the saved code-git-bundle manifest has no defined output location, bundle/output path overlap is not explicitly refused, deterministic repair lacks a persisted input identity rule, the 16 KiB normalized target limit conflicts with the 256 KiB configuration source limit, and several numeric/span/TOML rules remain narrative rather than closed wire semantics.
scope: Design-only review of CODE-PROOF-DESIGN-R2 against the prior CODE-DESIGN-R1 and the earlier bounded JSON/TOML configuration/span advice. Focused on retained descriptor lineage, bundle/object closure, pre-read and install budgets, fixed-batch repair, SHA-256 handoff compatibility, Decimal lexical/canonical semantics and raw/Unicode/line span coordinates. No source, schema, test, Git, provider, network, Vault or publication mutation.

accepted_or_well_bounded.evidence: R2 rejects the stale fb2cbcb rebasing direction and binds future work to the locally delivered Discovery successor; no implementation or legacy schema rewrite is authorized (lines 8-27).
The public workflow remains zero-egress and data-only: no network, subprocess, Git configuration, checkpoint URL, model, connector, operator or Vault access (lines 29-57).

One request, one acquisition intent and at most one completed observation, with normalized-only/raw distinction and no same-batch upgrade path, is a coherent replay boundary (lines 48-52, 181-207). The repair identity details still require closure below.

The type/space/decimal-length/NUL/body framing, separate body and framed hashes, selected SHA-1/SHA-256 OID width and no legacy 40-hex substitution are directionally correct (lines 23-27, 141-145). OID field and handoff width closure remains required below.

Shared retained descriptors, first-absence capture, complete-set observation, nonblocking checkout lock, duplicate lock descriptor and all-exit lineage precedence are the right safety model (lines 209-221). The overlapping bundle/output roots need an explicit refusal rule below.

Integer-only artifact JCS, string-typed decimal magnitudes, raw lexeme retention, Decimal cross-check, parser disagreement refusal and no partial verified node list preserve the legacy float boundary (lines 244-286). Exact lexical and coordinate wire grammar still needs to be frozen.

findings.title: code-git-bundle has no persisted output location or family
findings.evidence: R2 declares code-git-bundle as a document kind and says manifest.json is a saved envelope (lines 68-70, 124-138), then fixes the output to request.json, intent.json, observation.json and objects/configs/handoffs with no bundle/manifest path (lines 223-228).
findings.risk: A raw observation cannot be replayed from the output tree with a persisted manifest reference if the external manifest is not retained as a document. If intent.json embeds a bundle document, its kind/ID/reference semantics are ambiguous; if the external manifest remains authoritative, later status/config/handoff replay has an unbound input.
findings.required_closure: Choose one explicit layout before freeze, preferably a private 0600 bundle.json (or a declared manifests family), and specify its content-addressed filename/identity, exact request/profile binding, scan/permission rules, observation reference, idempotent repair behavior and orphan rejection. The 12 output families must then include and hash this path.

findings.title: Bundle root containment and output overlap are under-specified
findings.evidence: The bundle is only required to be below checkout/.work and outside the output code-evidence directory (lines 126-130); retained I/O rules do not state that bundle root and output root must be disjoint non-ancestor paths (lines 211-216).
findings.risk: A bundle directory at the batch root or another ancestor of code-evidence-v1 is outside the output directory yet output creation changes its complete sibling set. Symlink/alias spellings or an output descendant can make the source bundle and destination lineage share names or descriptors, producing unsafe classification or self-ingestion.
findings.required_closure: Require canonical descriptor-walk containment under checkout/.work with no symlink/reparse component; reject bundle root equal to, inside, or an ancestor of the output root and reject any input/output family overlap. Capture the bundle root and objects complete sets before classification and keep their descriptors/bytes verified through every output install.

findings.title: Deterministic repair does not state the persisted external-input identity
findings.evidence: R2 requires full validation before writes and says repeating observe with the same retained input repairs the missing suffix (lines 230-240), but does not require intent to retain a manifest/body input digest or define changed-path/missing-bundle behavior.
findings.risk: After an interruption, a caller can supply a different directory with the same batch ID. Without a persisted bundle manifest digest, declared OID/body digest set and mode-specific input identity, repair could install a different suffix or return an ambiguous semantic conflict.
findings.required_closure: Persist the complete acquisition-intent identity: mode, bundle envelope reference, manifest saved-byte SHA-256, ordered declared object records, per-object body SHA-256/size and target set. On repair, re-retain and revalidate the supplied bundle and refuse before any write when any identity, complete set, path spelling or mode differs. A normalized-only batch must reject any later bundle, as already intended.

findings.title: The per-target text cap conflicts with the configuration source cap
findings.evidence: R2 caps normalized text at 16 KiB per target (lines 111-116), while the configuration parser admits a 256 KiB source and a 2 MiB complete record (lines 266-269). Configuration consumes a raw blob from the complete raw observation (lines 246-248).
findings.risk: A valid configuration blob between 16 KiB and 256 KiB cannot simultaneously satisfy the stated complete raw observation/source-text outcome and the parser source cap. Implementations may silently reject valid requested configuration or weaken one bound; either changes the frozen contract.
findings.required_closure: State whether 16 KiB is only a normalized-text/handoff cap, whether configuration-role targets receive a separate raw/config cap, or whether the config source cap must be reduced. Define raw-byte versus normalized-byte accounting and make the selected result explicit in request limits, target outcomes and config eligibility.

findings.title: Declared object sums and transient atomic-install bytes need an explicit proof
findings.evidence: The profile lists 2048 objects, 8 MiB per object and 32 MiB total body limits, and says counts/declared sizes are checked before reading (lines 111-116), while output retention is bounded at 128 MiB including pending files (lines 223-228).
findings.risk: The design does not explicitly require the sum of all manifest body_size_bytes, metadata bytes, family file counts and pending temporary bytes to fit before opening any object body. Existing atomic installation briefly holds a private temporary body beside the final target; logical-only charging can exceed the stated pending-files cap.
findings.required_closure: Define a pre-read formula: object count, each declared size, sum declared bodies <=32 MiB, manifest <=1 MiB, tree-entry prospective count <=32768, and all request/intent/manifest/observation/config/handoff bytes plus atomic temp duplicates <=128 MiB. Reject on declarations/stat sizes before body reads; retain and verify temp/target sets and clean temp names on every exit.

findings.title: Numeric lexical and Decimal-context rules remain narrative rather than closed
findings.evidence: R2 names lexical validation, 128-byte lexemes, 64 significant digits, exponent 128, fixed notation, nonfinite and negative-zero refusal (lines 257-264), but does not publish the format-specific grammar or exact zero/sign/type rules.
findings.risk: JSON and TOML differ on plus signs, underscores, leading zeros and integer/decimal classification. A scanner and stdlib parser can disagree on `-0`, `+1`, `1e0`, `01`, `1_000`, `1.`, or `0E+128`; default Decimal context behavior can also accidentally round or erase sign/exponent provenance.
findings.required_closure: Carry forward the prior advice grammar and wire rules: RFC 8259 JSON number regex; explicit TOML decimal-integer/finite-float regex with underscore placement; typed integer versus decimal source classification; reject negative-zero lexemes and nonfinite forms; use context-free Decimal tuple conversion with no rounding; canonical fixed string/zero form; strict bool-versus-int distinction; retain original lexeme and raw span.

findings.title: Raw/codepoint/line-column coordinate contract needs exact definitions
findings.evidence: R2 requires half-open byte and original Unicode codepoint offsets, one-based line/column coordinates, CRLF treatment, raw hash and normalized snippet hash (lines 279-286), but does not define escaped-source coordinate units, column unit, tab policy or all container/implicit-table span cases.
findings.risk: For JSON escaped keys/strings, Unicode non-ASCII text and TOML escapes, decoded value coordinates differ from raw source token coordinates. Without a fixed rule, independently generated spans can hash the same bytes but report different positions; implicit TOML tables and multiline arrays can produce synthetic or missing spans.
findings.required_closure: Define offsets and columns over the strict decoded source string before newline normalization, in Python Unicode scalar/codepoint units (not UTF-16 or grapheme/display columns); raw token spans always slice original bytes. State CRLF as two bytes/codepoints and one line advance, bare CR refusal, tabs as one codepoint, escaped-token/raw-token boundaries, JSON root/container spans, TOML header/key/scalar/array/inline-table spans, and no synthetic implicit-table value span.

findings.title: TOML multiline and key-redefinition boundaries are not fully frozen
findings.evidence: R2 excludes multiline strings and arrays-of-tables but admits arrays, inline tables, ordinary tables and dotted keys (lines 250-255); no rule says whether multiline arrays/comments or implicit-table promotion are accepted and how their spans map.
findings.risk: tomllib accepts syntax outside the prose subset. A scanner may accept a multiline array while the span model assumes single-line values, or disagree with parser shape on implicit table creation, dotted-key/table redefinition and quoted-key equivalence.
findings.required_closure: Choose and publish either a fully supported multiline-array/comment subset with exact spans, or reject multiline arrays and every other out-of-subset construct before stdlib cross-check. Specify decoded-key collision/redefinition behavior, implicit-table node emission and table/header/key spans, then add vectors for equivalent quoted/dotted spellings and all duplicate paths.

findings.title: SHA-256 handoff compatibility is stated but not wire-bound
findings.evidence: R2 explicitly permits 64-hex Git objects and rejects legacy 40-hex substitution (lines 23-27, 141-145), but the source-handoff field set is not specified and the legacy code manifest still only accepts 40-hex commits in the existing boundary.
findings.risk: A phase-1 handoff can accidentally omit object_format or emit a 64-hex commit into a downstream field whose schema assumes 40 hex, causing unsafe truncation, implicit conversion or an unusable handoff. The phase-1 no-legacy-manifest rule alone does not guarantee successor adapter compatibility.
findings.required_closure: Freeze source-handoff fields that carry object_format and exact-width commit/tree/blob OIDs, raw/body/framed hashes, logical target path, source bytes reference, normalized metadata and configuration spans. Mark the handoff as successor-only and reject any legacy manifest/capture adapter path until the later CODE-CANONICAL schema explicitly supports SHA-256.

required_freeze_actions: Define and hash the complete 12-path (or amended) CODE-PROOF output allowlist, including the persisted code-git-bundle manifest path.
Close bundle root containment/overlap, persisted repair identity, object declaration preflight and transient atomic-install accounting before implementation.
Resolve the 16 KiB normalized target versus 256 KiB config source contract.
Promote the prior JSON/TOML numeric grammar and span-coordinate advice into frozen schema/profile semantics, including TOML multiline/redefinition rules.
Define SHA-256-capable source-handoff fields independently of the legacy 40-hex code manifest.
timestamp_basis: Tool-observed current UTC from date -u; no retrospective review-start time is asserted.
